title: Commercial Construction Newcastle: Project Manager vs Builder, Who Does What?
metaTitle: Construction Project Manager vs Builder Newcastle | YOS
metaDescription: Understand client-side project management and builder responsibilities for a Newcastle commercial construction or office fit out project. Use a scope checklist.
excerpt: Clarify who manages client decisions, who delivers the work and who handles specialist approvals. A practical role and scope guide for Newcastle commercial projects.
author: Your Office Space
body:
A client-side commercial construction project manager coordinates the business owner's project brief, decisions, consultants and agreed delivery workstream. The appointed builder delivers building work under its contract. For a Newcastle office fit out or broader commercial construction project, defining those roles before appointments helps the client understand what each proposal actually covers.

Your Office Space provides client-side project management. Building and trade work is performed by appointed contractors. This guide is a practical scope comparison, rather than a statement that every project has the same contracts, approvals or delivery structure.

## Start with a responsibility map

Write down the outcomes the business needs and identify who is appointed to deliver each part. Include the design, approval inputs, procurement, construction, client decisions, furniture and handover workstreams. If a role is unassigned, record it as an open action rather than assuming another party will cover it.

The following table is a briefing starting point. Actual duties, authority and reporting arrangements must be established in the appointments and contracts for your project.

| Role | Typical focus to clarify | Confirm in the appointment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Business owner or client | Business requirements, funding and approvals of client decisions | Decision maker, approval limits and response process |
| Client-side project manager | Coordination of the agreed client workstream and project information | Scope, reporting, authority, exclusions and fee |
| Designer or specialist consultant | Design and specialist advice within the appointed discipline | Deliverables, coordination and responsibility for revisions |
| Builder or appointed contractor | Delivery of the contracted building or trade work | Inclusions, exclusions, programme, site responsibilities and handover |
| Certifier, where required | Statutory certification duties within the appointment | Required inspections, certificates and applicant responsibilities |
| Furniture supplier and installer | Specified products, delivery and installation scope | Lead times, access, placement, completion and packaging handling |

NSW Government guidance distinguishes a certifier's certification duties from the builder's work. Confirm the appropriate certification and approval pathway with your appointed advisers; a project manager does not replace those specialist roles.

[Read NSW Government guidance on what certifiers do](https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/appointing-a-certifier/what-certifiers-do)

## What should a project management proposal explain?

Look for a clear starting point and finishing point. Does the engagement begin with the brief, after design, during contractor procurement or once works have started? Does it include handover coordination and follow-up actions? A proposal described only as project management leaves too much unresolved.

Ask how decisions, budgets, programme updates and changes will be recorded. Identify who can approve expenditure, instruct variations or commit the client. Coordination alone does not establish authority to sign contracts or approve additional costs.

## Compare proposals on the same scope

Two management fees are not directly comparable if one includes procurement and handover while the other covers progress reporting only. First align the workstreams, then compare fees, assumptions, exclusions, duration and the resources proposed.

Keep contractor quotes separate from project management fees, consultant fees and other project allowances. Check whether furniture, services, landlord requirements, defects follow-up and documentation are included or separately appointed. Record unpriced items so they remain visible in the overall budget.

## Include Newcastle site constraints early

For a Newcastle CBD tenancy, ask the landlord or building manager about loading, lift bookings, access windows and the rules relevant to the proposed works. For a site in Maryville, Lake Macquarie or elsewhere in the Hunter, check its actual arrangements using the same approach.

Describe whether staff need to keep operating during the project, which areas can be isolated and who manages client access decisions. Do not assume that after-hours work, uninterrupted operations or a particular completion date is included without agreement.

[Plan an office fit out in Newcastle](/office-fitout)

## Make handover part of the brief

A target opening date needs more than a calendar entry. Identify required completion documents, specialist sign-offs where applicable, client training, defects records and responsibility for resolving remaining items. Confirm which tasks must be complete before occupation with the appointed project team.

Furniture installation and the business move should be coordinated with the site's readiness and agreed access arrangements. A separately agreed furniture scope can connect those decisions without obscuring the builder's or consultant's responsibilities.

[Use the office fit out handover checklist](/blog/office-fitout-handover-checklist)

## Frequently asked questions

### Does a client-side project manager build the project?

YOS provides client-side project management. The appointed builder and trade contractors deliver the building work under their contracts. The agreed responsibility map identifies how the workstreams connect.

### Can I appoint a project manager if I already have a builder?

You can discuss a coordination brief at that stage. Share the current appointments, contracts, programme and outstanding decisions so the management scope can be assessed without assuming another party's authority.

### Do all commercial projects need the same approvals?

No. The proposed work, site and applicable requirements determine the approval and certification pathway. Obtain project-specific advice from the appropriately appointed specialists.

### How should I compare project management fees?

Compare the scope, project stage, duration, reporting, authority and exclusions first. Then assess the proposed fee alongside the separate contractor, consultant and other project costs.

### Can YOS coordinate office furniture as well?

Yes. Furniture planning, supply and installation coordination can be considered under a separately agreed scope, alongside the project programme and site's access requirements.
